metadata.title: This Week: Done, and Still a Draft
metadata.register: Professional, polite, simple -- a real progress update, not overhyped, per the user's explicit tone request.
metadata.note: A CLI-explainer weekly recap -- a NEW week's log, separate from the earlier weekly-recap builds (weekly-recap, -catbot, -suffolk, -never-forgets, -tutor, -mcphs). Same story spine as those builds (B00 cold open -> problem -> ask -> code -> output -> change -> code -> output -> lesson -> handoff -> outro; real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat; one required revision cycle). weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run; v1 is a flat list of four entries, v2 adds a status to each (published / attended / first draft / produced) and prints a finished-vs-draft count -- chosen because the user asked for an honest update that says the promotion-strategy document is only a first draft. THE STRATEGY DRAFT IS NOT DESCRIBED beyond 'a first draft' (user instruction): its graphic uses blank placeholder bars, not real content. HOMES OF HOPE VISUALS ARE ABSTRACT (user instruction): a calendar and a house outline only -- no photos, no people shapes. Video count: the user's kickoff says 'four videos', while the user's own note beneath it says to use 'two videos, each exported in 16:9 and 9:16, four files in total so the narration is accurate'; that accurate wording is used (this session produced the hotel-phone-helper video and this recap, each in two formats). Disclosed substitutions carried forward: (1) af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default voice/handle; (2) rendered through run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py. Self-intro ('Hi, I'm Agrima') folds into B00's own narration per the cli-explainer skill's convention. All items are the user's own self-reported account. No footage exists -- every visual is a generated Manim graphic.

beats.role_note: the real weekly_recap_v1.py output, visualized as four same-weight cards (the three parts: writing, Homes of Hope, video production)
beats.narration_text: Run it, and here's the week. One article on Substack, The Hotel Phone Gets a Helper, about how AI voice assistants are answering hotel calls at any hour, and giving front desk teams more time for guests. Meetings for Homes of Hope, a project that supports marginalized girls in India with a safe home, education, and support. A first draft of strategies for promoting the Homes of Hope documentary movie, written together with Yatra, so the girls' stories can reach a wider audience. And two videos on Brutalist, each taken through planning, review, approvals, and export, in sixteen by nine and nine by sixteen: four files in total.
beats.visual_intent: four same-weight cards: mock Substack header ('The Hotel Phone Gets a Helper'); a meeting/calendar card for Homes of Hope; a document card 'Draft: documentary promotion strategies (with Yatra)' with blank placeholder bars; two videos each split into 16:9 + 9:16, all checked

beats.role_note: the revision ask -- add a status to each item and count
beats.narration_text: But a flat list hides one thing: the draft isn't finished. So: add a status to each item, and count them.
